text:
maria: Heads up — I've been seeing steady RSS growth on prod kv-cache when contexts go beyond ~8k tokens. Putting notes + a quick proposal here.

kevin: repro? logs?

maria: repro is a sustained stream of long-chat requests. Quick numbers from yesterday's canary (p3.2xlarge):
```
repro command: ./tools/loadtest --profile=kv --ctx=10000 --qps=80 --duration=2h
pprof summary (heap): inuse_space=4.2GB, alloc_objects=3.1M, free_slots=1.2M, avg_fill=37%
observed growth: ~+1.8GB RSS over 2h (no incoming model size change)
```

samir: sounds like fragmentation — allocator rounds small free regions up to 512B block size, then lots of partially filled blocks pile up with long-context churn.

jia: +1. Do you have a flamegraph or timeline showing when blocks become cold vs hot?

maria: timeline attached (short link): https://internal/trace/az12/kv-frag-177999 — pattern: hot streams create many small KV entries, then as users scroll/extend contexts some entries become obsolete but the block-level free list has large holes.

samir: two levers: 1) reduce min-block to 256B for small entry buckets (trade: more metadata / pointer overhead), 2) background incremental repack that migrates live entries out of high-frag blocks.

matt: what's the perf hit for repack? we care tail latency.

maria: measured micro-run: single-threaded repack of 5k entries -> CPU ~0.6 core, moves 5k/sec, p50 extra latency ~+12ms for a write path if not careful. But we can run on low-priority background worker to avoid affecting p99 for inference.

jia: propose hybrid strategy: minor coalesce on free events (cheap, immediate), plus time-sliced repack windows when node CPU < 40% and network idle. Pseudoconfig: 
```
kv.repack.enabled = true
kv.repack.max_moves_per_window = 5000
kv.repack.window_ms = 1000
kv.block.min_size = 256   # for small buckets only
kv.repack.frag_threshold = 0.60  # >60% fragmentation triggers repack
kv.repack.age_threshold_ms = 1800000 # only repack blocks older than 30m
```

kevin: can we A/B this? need a canary plan + metrics. Also want safety: if repack causes OOM or lat spikes, auto-disable.

maria: plan: canary on 2 nodes tonight with kv.repack.max_moves_per_window=2500 first, collect metrics for 4h, then scale. We'll gate by reclaimed_bytes/hour and p99 inference latency.

matt: add these observables: fragmentation_ratio, reclaimed_bytes_hour, repack_moves, repack_cpu_secs, p50/p99 inference latency, rss_delta_hour. Also set alert if p99 > baseline + 15%.

perf-bot: latest baseline (last 24h): fragmentation_ratio=0.62, reclaimed_bytes_hour=4.3MB, p99_infer=178ms, rss_growth_rate=0.9GB/h

kevin: good. who runs tonight?

maria: I can run it. Will create a rollout PR with feature flag kv.repack.v1 and a quick kill-switch.

lee: +1 for the flag approach. tag me on the PR, I'll help review infra bits. :white_check_mark:

samir: do we have unit/integration tests to ensure repack doesn't reorder KV indices or break LRU semantics?

maria: not yet — I'll add tests that simulate long append/trim patterns and validate correctness + latency harness.

kevin: if you push the PR, add a short runbook for rolling back and metrics dashboard link.

maria: will do. starting the canary at 23:30 PT unless anyone objects.

lee: no objections.

samir: leave a note if we need to revert.

maria: thanks all — will post results in this thread after the canary. :rocket:
